title: runtime-anchors-and-verified-performance-refresh-playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define and publish a stable 'runtime anchor' artifact and an automated refresh playbook for Redwood-verified performance profiles that capture latency, throughput, and cost characteristics for each onboarded model and version. Scope: building the artifact format (runtime-anchor), automating profile ingestion from benchmark pipelines, adding metadata for pinning and rollback decisions, and defining operational runbooks for profile drift and refresh cadence. Out of scope: low-level kernel optimization work and new benchmarking infra — we will consume outputs from the existing benchmark pipeline.
background: We publish verified performance profiles to let customers pin model versions to predictable latency/cost targets. Current gaps discovered in audits: (1) profiles lack a compact runtime anchor that encodes the runtime configuration used for measurements (GPU type, kernel set, quantization flags, sequence-sampling distribution), which makes automated compatibility decisions brittle; (2) profile refreshes are manual and inconsistent across regions/variants; (3) rollback and canary criteria are underspecified. This ticket creates a canonical artifact plus a refresh/rollback playbook to reduce manual work and improve reliability.
goals: Define a machine-readable runtime-anchor spec and register it with the perf-catalog
Automate profile ingestion from the benchmarking pipeline with anchor validation
Publish a playbook for scheduled refresh, drift detection, and emergency rollbacks
Expose anchor metadata in the Console and API so customers can pin by anchor IDs
Add clear cost-normalized metrics (tokens/sec, median p50/p95 latency, cost-per-1k tokens) to each published profile
non_goals: Changing model selection criteria used by the benchmark pipeline
Rewriting kernel-selection code in the runtime
Implementing a monetization change to pricing plans
acceptance_criteria: A JSON schema for runtime-anchor is published to the performance-catalog repo and has been reviewed by runtime and infra teams
Benchmark pipeline emits runtime-anchor metadata for every verified profile in the staging bucket
Automated ingestion job validates anchors, normalizes cost metrics, and publishes profiles to staging with clear 'anchor_id' and 'profile_version' fields
Console shows anchor_id, hardware family, quantization profile, and normalized cost; API returns anchor metadata when requesting profiles
A runbook exists that defines scheduled refresh frequency, drift detection thresholds, canary rollout steps, and immediate rollback triggers
At least one end-to-end test: onboard a test model, publish profile, simulate drift in throughput, and execute rollback policy in a staging environment
tasks: Draft runtime-anchor JSON schema with fields: anchor_id, hardware_family, kernel_set_hash, quantization_profile, sequence_distribution_signature, benchmark_tool_versions
Iterate schema with runtime and infra in a 1-hour design review
Add anchor metadata emission into existing benchmark ETL (coord with bench team)
Build ingestion lambda that validates anchors and writes canonical profile to perf-catalog staging
Update Console profile view to surface anchor metadata and a 'pin to anchor' button
Design playbook doc: scheduled refresh policy, automated drift detection heuristics (p50 shift > 15% or cost-per-token delta > 10%), and canary rollout steps
Create acceptance tests and CI job that runs a toy onboarding + publish + rollback scenario
Publish RFC describing anchor semantics and pinning implications for customers
Coordinate with Legal/Security on metadata fields to avoid leaking internal identifiers
risks: Anchor schema becomes too verbose and slows ingestion — mitigate by limiting required fields and adding optional extension map
Bench pipeline inconsistencies across regions produce anchors that are not comparable — mitigate via canonical normalization step and region tag
Customers pin to anchors that become invalid after hardware refreshes — mitigate by adding expiry and recommended replacement anchors
Automated rollback triggers could be noisy and flip-flop under transient load — mitigate with cooldown windows and multi-metric confirmation
out_of_scope_notes: Per-model privacy tagging and customer-specific benchmarks (handled in separate enterprise project)
Experimenting with new cost-accounting models beyond cost-per-1k tokens in this sprint
